title: Xiaohongshu note.json
description: One note, as `collect.py` writes it into <noteId>/note.json. Everything here is content an agent reads; how the note was collected (tab, media URLs, download state) lives in downloads.json beside it, and the thread in comments.json. A field that neither source prints is null rather than absent, so a missing IP location or update time is distinguishable from a collector that forgot to look.

noteId.description: The note's ID, parsed from the URL.

url.description: The page URL verbatim, query string included — the access token in it is what makes the link reusable.

author.description: Null only in a file migrated from the pre-v2 layout, whose collector never stored the author; the warning in the file says so.

authorId.description: The numeric profile id in the author's /user/profile/<id> link.

ipLocation.description: The IP location the footer prints after the date, e.g. "河南". Null when the note prints none.

publishedAt.description: Publish time, in +08:00. Taken from the state's own `time` when the state was readable, otherwise decoded from the first 8 hex digits of the note ID. The printed date ("08-01", "4天前") cannot be placed on a calendar on its own, so it is never the source.

updatedAt.description: Last edit time, in +08:00, from the state's `lastUpdateTime`. This is the primary evidence for whether a stored copy of the note is stale. It equals `publishedAt` on a note that was never edited (measured on 6a6df219), and it is null when the state could not be read — the page prints the day a note was edited ("编辑于 2025-09-24") but never the second, so the DOM cannot supply it either.

capturedFrom.description: Which source the metadata block came from. `state` is the page's server-rendered store, `dom` the selectors in locators.yaml. A `dom` read is not wrong, but it carries no `updatedAt` and no share count, so it is worth knowing which one produced a thin file.

stats.description: The interaction bar. `shares` is filled from the state's `interactInfo.shareCount` and is null only on a DOM-only read — the web detail view has no share element at all.

tags.description: Topic names without the #/[话题] markers the page prints around them. Null only in a file migrated from the pre-v2 layout, which stored no tags.

content.description: The note body as plain text.

warnings.description: Problems worth reporting, including a one-line summary per unfinished download (the detail is in downloads.json).
